original_claim_summary: EPA's 2026 rescission of the 2009 Endangerment Finding is dated July 14 and linked to a 12-billion-ton CO2 increase by 2040, along with repeal of clean-energy credits.

source_urls.access_notes: EPA rule summary reviewed; it gives the finalization date and scope.
supports: EPA finalized the rescission on February 12, 2026.
EPA also repealed subsequent GHG standards for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty highway vehicles and engines; its page says traditional-pollutant rules were unaffected.
EDF criticized the rescission and said it would lead to more pollution and harms.

source_urls.access_notes: Official final rule; published February 18, with an April 20 effective date.
supports: The rule rescinds the 2009 findings and repeals GHG emission standards for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty vehicles and engines.

supported_facts: The rescission was finalized February 12, 2026, not July 14.
The final rule withdrew the 2009 Endangerment Finding and vehicle/engine GHG standards; this describes EPA's regulatory action, not its eventual climate effects.
unsupported_original_claims: The cited February 2026 EDF statement does not support the stored 1.5-billion-ton-by-2030 / 12-billion-ton-by-2040 figures or the combined clean-energy-credit claim. The returned EDF statement instead describes harms qualitatively; no transparent analysis for the stored figures was established in this packet.
The entry date July 14, 2026 is inconsistent with the official finalization date.
The quotes attributed to Zeldin and the Kolbert investigation are not verified by these exact sources as part of this discrete final-rule event.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: EPA rescinds 2009 greenhouse-gas Endangerment Finding and vehicle standards
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: EPA finalized the rescission of the 2009 greenhouse-gas Endangerment Finding on February 12, 2026 and repealed subsequent highway-vehicle and engine GHG standards. The stored emissions projection should be omitted pending a source that directly explains its methodology and policy assumptions.

exact_evidence_gap: No source reviewed tied the 12-billion-ton estimate to this February 2026 final rule; a separate older clean-car rollback projection cannot be assumed to measure this action.
disposition_rationale: Retain the documented regulatory event with its correct date and scope; do not present the stored emissions estimate as an established consequence.

original_claim_summary: The June 1, 2026 CMS rule allegedly excludes cancer patients from a medical-frailty exemption unless chemotherapy symptoms meet a specific work-impairment test, causing coverage loss.

source_urls.access_notes: CMS fact sheet reviewed; describes the interim final rule and exemptions.
supports: CMS issued an interim final rule with comment period on June 1, 2026.
The rule defines medical-frailty/special-medical-needs exemptions and links them to significant impairment in complying with community-engagement requirements.

source_urls.access_notes: Article text excerpt reviewed; no final eligibility decision is reported for Brandon.
supports: AP identifies Jennifer Brandon of North Carolina as a cancer patient concerned that treatment-related exhaustion and memory challenges may not qualify automatically.
AP says she would have to attest and later prove that the symptoms significantly impair her ability to meet the requirements.

supported_facts: CMS issued the rule on June 1, 2026 and included medical-frailty exemptions.
AP reported Brandon's concern about whether treatment side effects would meet the rule's impairment standard; she had not been told that she was ineligible.
unsupported_original_claims: The entry calls the rule final; CMS labels it an interim final rule with a comment period.
The sources do not establish that Brandon was told she would not qualify, that she was denied an exemption, or that her coverage was terminated.
The claims that the rule shocked advocates and imposes burdens for which coverage loss means death are not supported by these two sources as specific facts about Brandon.
The original assertion that chemotherapy symptoms must be proved in a particular adjudicated case overstates a future verification requirement as an actual outcome.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: CMS Medicaid rule sets a medical-frailty test that worries a cancer patient
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: CMS's June 1, 2026 interim final rule ties a medical-frailty exemption to significant impairment in meeting community-engagement requirements. AP reported that Jennifer Brandon, who experiences exhaustion and memory problems during cancer treatment, was concerned those symptoms might not qualify; AP did not report an eligibility denial.

exact_evidence_gap: No reviewed source establishes how a state ultimately assessed Brandon, whether she applied for the exemption, or whether she lost Medicaid coverage.
disposition_rationale: Use the rule and AP account for the exemption standard and reported concern only; do not claim a completed denial or coverage loss.

original_claim_summary: Melania Trump's January 19, 2025 token launch allegedly caused $TRUMP to crash nearly 50%, wiped $30 billion, involved an insider-funded pump-and-dump, and reached a $13 billion fully diluted value.

source_urls.access_notes: Contemporaneous market report reviewed through indexed article text.
supports: Melania Trump launched the $MELANIA token on January 19, 2025.
The report says $TRUMP fell about 48% in the immediate reaction.
The Guardian reported that roughly $7.5 billion in $TRUMP market capitalization was erased in about ten minutes after the launch.

supported_facts: $MELANIA was announced/launched on January 19, one day after $TRUMP debuted.
Contemporaneous reports describe an immediate $TRUMP decline of roughly 48% and a roughly $7.5 billion market-cap reduction in one report.
unsupported_original_claims: The cited reporting does not support a $30 billion value loss.
The sources do not establish a family pump-and-dump or that insiders sold $TRUMP proceeds to fund $MELANIA purchases.
The sources reviewed do not establish Ran Neuner's alleged advance knowledge/profit or the exact $13 billion fully diluted peak; token valuation depends on metric and timestamp.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: $TRUMP falls after Melania Trump launches $MELANIA token
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: Melania Trump launched $MELANIA on January 19, 2025. The Block reported an immediate roughly 48% drop in $TRUMP, while The Guardian reported about $7.5 billion in market capitalization erased in roughly ten minutes. These reports do not establish the claimed $30 billion loss or insider funding allegations.

exact_evidence_gap: No credible source reviewed supports the $30 billion loss, the asserted insider funding mechanism, or the stated peak valuation on a clearly specified fully diluted basis.
disposition_rationale: Retain the narrow, contemporaneously reported market reaction; treat allegations and inconsistent token valuation metrics separately unless directly sourced.

original_claim_summary: The entry attributes a $793 billion Medicaid reduction and 10.3 million additional uninsured people to the enacted July 4, 2025 law, combines it with subsidy expiration, and describes 18.5 million affected adults.

source_urls.access_notes: CBO's enacted-law estimate reviewed; it covers Public Law 119-21 and reports impacts against the specified baseline.
supports: CBO estimated that Medicaid provisions in the enacted law increase the number of people without health insurance by 7.5 million in 2034.
CBO reported $886.8 billion in deficit reduction from the Medicaid chapter over 2025-2034; this is not interchangeable with a federal Medicaid spending-cut figure.

source_urls.access_notes: CBO estimate for a prior House-passed version, not the final enacted statute.
supports: The House-passed bill's Medicaid provisions were estimated to increase the uninsured by 7.8 million in 2034; this is a distinct legislative version and score.

source_urls.access_notes: KFF compares estimate vintages and baselines; its Medicaid spending figure is explicitly attributed to its CBO-baseline comparison.
supports: KFF reports a roughly $911 billion projected reduction in federal Medicaid spending over ten years for the enacted law, with its stated baseline and methodology.

supported_facts: CBO's enacted-law Medicaid estimate is 7.5 million more uninsured people in 2034; the separate House-passed estimate was 7.8 million.
The enacted-law uninsured estimate differs from the House-passed score; the entries must not combine versions or baselines.
unsupported_original_claims: The reviewed enacted-law CBO estimate does not support 10.3 million additional uninsured people by 2034.
The $793 billion and 10.3 million figures are not the final-law estimate in the cited CBO report.
The 18.5-million figure and the combined 16-million total are not established by these cited estimates as written.
The record's distinct enhanced-subsidy expiration estimate should not be merged into the Medicaid chapter's score.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: Enacted 2025 reconciliation law projected to add 7.5 million uninsured through Medicaid provisions
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: CBO estimated that the Medicaid provisions of Public Law 119-21 would increase the number of uninsured people by 7.5 million in 2034. Earlier estimates for the House-passed bill differ and should be labeled separately; do not attribute the earlier $793 billion or 10.3 million figures to the enacted law.

exact_evidence_gap: The supplied $793 billion / 10.3 million pairing is not reconciled to the final-law CBO score; the original combined estimate also lacks a source separating Medicaid effects from the expiration of enhanced marketplace credits.
disposition_rationale: Replace the mixed-version numbers with the enacted-law estimate and preserve distinct baselines and program effects.

original_claim_summary: Interior's February 2025 order allegedly opened monuments to extraction, and officials had already set boundary cuts across six named monuments by April.

source_urls.access_notes: Interior's February 3, 2025 departmental orders reviewed; they direct reviews and expansion of domestic energy/mineral development.
supports: Secretary Doug Burgum issued orders to expedite energy and mineral development reviews on February 3, 2025.

source_urls.access_notes: Report text was reviewed via indexed text; its sources were anonymous administration officials.
supports: The April 24 report said officials were considering boundary reductions at six western national monuments, including Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante, partly to open areas to mining and oil extraction.
The report describes consideration, not a completed boundary change.

supported_facts: Interior launched energy/mineral development reviews in February 2025.
The Washington Post reported in April that reductions at six western monuments were under consideration; no completed reduction was established in that report.
unsupported_original_claims: The sources do not establish that the six monuments were opened to extraction or that reductions had been decided.

Claims about more than 3.2 million acres, prior Trump-term reductions, uranium/coal reserves, record energy output, and specific watershed or archaeological impacts require separate direct sources and are not supported by these two sources.
The anonymous sourcing and reported consideration should not be represented as an official adopted boundary plan.

narrow_corrected_claim.title: Interior officials reportedly consider reducing boundaries of six western monuments
narrow_corrected_claim.claim: The Washington Post reported on April 24, 2025 that administration officials were considering reductions at six western national monuments to facilitate mining and oil development. The reported reviews were under consideration, not completed policy changes.

exact_evidence_gap: The report relied on unnamed officials and does not establish a signed decision, final monument list adopted by Interior, or any completed opening of protected land to extraction.
disposition_rationale: Retain the sourced report as a reported internal consideration, attribute its anonymous sourcing, and omit effects or implementation not established.
